facts.fact: Nielsen's Ad-Supported Gauge, as cited by Adwave, reports that 73.6% of all U.S. TV time included advertising in Q2 2025.
facts.quote: Specifically, 73.6% of all TV time includes advertising, whether viewers are watching streaming services, cable, or broadcast.

facts.fact: Ad-supported share of U.S. TV viewing rose 1.2 percentage points from Q1 2025, which was 72.4%.
facts.quote: Ad-supported viewing rose 1.2 percentage points from Q1 2025 (72.4%)

facts.fact: Within ad-supported TV, streaming accounts for approximately 45% of viewing, according to the Adwave page citing Nielsen data.
facts.quote: Within ad-supported TV, streaming accounts for approximately 45%, followed by cable (29%) and broadcast (26%)

facts.fact: Within ad-supported TV, cable accounts for approximately 29% of viewing.
facts.quote: Cable accounts for about 29%, while broadcast represents roughly 26%.

facts.fact: Only 26.4% of U.S. TV viewing happens on ad-free tiers and content.
facts.quote: Only 26.4% of TV viewing happens on ad-free tiers and content

facts.fact: May 2025 was the first time streaming surpassed broadcast and cable combined in TV viewing.
facts.quote: May 2025 marked the first time streaming surpassed broadcast + cable combined

facts.fact: Total U.S. TV viewing dipped 9% quarter-over-quarter while ad-supported viewing still grew.
facts.quote: ad-supported viewing grew even as total TV viewing dipped 9% quarter-over-quarter

facts.fact: YouTube alone represents over 10% of all U.S. TV viewing, and it is almost entirely ad-supported.
facts.quote: YouTube alone represents over 10% of all TV viewing and is almost entirely ad-supported.

facts.fact: The average U.S. household subscribes to 4 or more streaming services.
facts.quote: The average U.S. household now subscribes to 4+ streaming services.

facts.fact: Netflix reported that over 40% of new subscribers in ad-supported markets choose the ad tier.
facts.quote: Netflix reported that 40%+ of new subscribers in ad-supported markets choose the ad tier.

facts.fact: Adwave recommends beginning a TV test with a $100-$200 budget and running it for 2 weeks.
facts.quote: Begin with $100-$200 to gather initial data. Run for 2 weeks to capture viewing patterns.

facts.fact: Industry analysts, as cited by Adwave, project ad-supported viewing will reach 75%+ of total TV time by 2026.
facts.quote: Industry analysts project ad-supported viewing will reach 75%+ of total TV time by 2026.

facts.fact: Nielsen's Ad-Supported Gauge was launched in 2025.
facts.quote: Nielsen's Ad-Supported Gauge, launched in 2025

facts.fact: Adwave states that small businesses can run TV campaigns starting at $30 a day.
facts.quote: small businesses can run TV campaigns starting at $30 a day

facts.fact: Adwave states that CPMs typically range from $15 to $35.
facts.quote: CPMs typically range from $15-$35, meaning $100 can reach 3,000-6,000 households.

facts.fact: According to Nielsen, 73.6% of U.S. TV time includes advertising.
facts.quote: 73.6% of U.S. TV time includes advertising

facts.fact: According to Nielsen Gauge, streaming accounts for 47.3% of total U.S. TV time.
facts.quote: Streaming accounts for 47.3% of total TV time

facts.fact: According to Netflix earnings, 40% or more of new subscribers in ad-supported markets choose the ad tier.
facts.quote: 40%+ of new subscribers in ad-supported markets choose ad tier

facts.fact: According to eMarketer, free ad-supported streaming grew 25% or more year over year.
facts.quote: Free ad-supported streaming grew 25%+ YoY

facts.fact: According to eMarketer, U.S. CTV advertising is projected to reach $30 billion or more in 2025.
facts.quote: U.S. CTV advertising projected to reach $30+ billion in 2025

facts.fact: According to Parks Associates, 85% of U.S. households have at least one smart TV.
facts.quote: 85% of U.S. households have at least one smart TV

facts.fact: The page projects that ad-supported viewing will reach 75% or more by 2026, without naming a source.
facts.quote: ad-supported viewing is projected to reach 75%+ by 2026

facts.fact: The page defines ad-supported TV as content where advertising appears during viewing and excludes ad-free subscription tiers.
facts.quote: It does not include ad-free subscription tiers.

facts.fact: Nielsen's Ad-Supported Gauge uses the traditional Gauge panel methodology combined with automatic content recognition (ACR) data from smart TVs and set-top boxes.
facts.quote: combined with automatic content recognition (ACR) data from smart TVs and set-top boxes
